entries.condition: still vs 90th flight frame from the same fixed camera; temporal behaviour inferred from source (sky.ts static hash12 jitter, vegetation.ts count thinning at 2000/3500/5000 m, game.ts PMREM refresh every 5 s)
entries.evidence: Cloud grain is a fixed per-pixel dither (hash12(gl_FragCoord) jitter at 0.6 render scale) that does not move with the clouds; the aircraft moved 470 px between still and flight without frame-to-frame smear, but vegetation tiles switch instance count at 2000/3500/5000 m and castShadow at 1800 m, and the environment map is rebuilt every 5 s.
entries.defect: Static dither grain on clouds and threshold-based tree/shadow popping plus a 5 s environment-map rebuild hitch are temporal defects a player sees in ordinary flight.
entries.fix: Replace the static jitter with blue-noise + temporal accumulation or a 3x3 depth-aware upsample, fade instance counts over 300 m instead of stepping, and time-slice the PMREM refresh over 6 frames.

entries.condition: HUD/telemetry consistency of the posed aircraft (112 KIAS, 1444 ft, +550 fpm, heading 326) and plausibility of the flight log (flighttest.json) against a 2.3 t bush floatplane
entries.evidence: HUD values match metrics telemetry (57.8 m/s = 112 kt, 440 m = 1444 ft); the log gives liftoff 64.7 KIAS at 20.8 s, 759 fpm at 95 KIAS, 109 KIAS at 74% power still accelerating (Vmax solves to ~138 kt), 45-degree turn 8.7 deg/s at 120 kt (theory 9.1), stall 53 KIAS at alpha 15.5 deg - all within DHC-2 class figures.
entries.defect: The approach ended in a nose-over to -76 deg pitch / -82 deg bank on land with no crash state (physics.ts has only two wheel contact points, both at x = -0.9 behind the CG), and post-stall the aircraft mushed at alpha 11-13 deg for 15 s with a +/-10 deg pitch phugoid.
entries.fix: Add the two bow-wheel contact points (2.3, -2.35, +/-1.25), steepen post-stall lift loss (3.5 -> 6.0 per rad), raise Cm_q from -18 to -22, cut elevator power 0.8 -> 0.45, and add a crash/reset state.

entries.condition: compare near, mid and far detail: island trees at 1-2 km, skyline at 4-6 km, far shore at 8+ km

flightModel.verdict: The aerodynamic envelope is plausible for a 2.3 t DHC-2-class floatplane (stall 53-57 kt, cruise 109-138 kt, climb ~750 fpm, turn rate within 5% of theory). Control authority is excessive (steady roll rate ~146 deg/s at 60 m/s; 27 deg pitch-up with a +3600 fpm zoom in 4 s from cruise), post-stall behaviour is too benign and under-damped, the ground model has no forward support so any land contact nose-overs, there is no crash/reset state, and the water contact geometry is 7-17 cm below the visual hull while the rendered frames show the hull entirely above the water. The chase camera has a vector-aliasing bug that displaces its look target by 6x the spring acceleration.

performance.note: Real-GPU FPS was not measurable on this VM: frames were rendered by SwiftShader (CPU) and 'renderMs' only measures JS submission time; category 27 is scored from draw calls, triangles, memory and pipeline structure.
biggestCosts: Shadow passes: CSM with 3 cascades x 2048^2 PCFSoftShadowMap; vegetation tiles cast within 1800 m and building tiles within 2600 m, so every tree/building is drawn 4x; maxFar grows to cam.y*9 (up to 12 km). Roughly two thirds of the 9-11 M triangles and 1,300-1,600 draw calls are shadow work.

Water: a 70 km plane (frustumCulled=false, renderOrder 5, drawn last) whose fragment shader evaluates 4 noised() layers, 5 fbm3 (15 value-noise) + 1 vnoise, 3 texture fetches, PCFSoft on 3 cascades and env-map IBL per pixel; with logarithmicDepthBuffer the shader writes gl_FragDepth, so early-Z cannot skip water hidden behind terrain.
logarithmicDepthBuffer: true forces gl_FragDepth in every material and disables early-Z / hierarchical-Z for the whole scene, so city and vegetation overdraw is paid in full.

Sky: 24-step cloud ray march with a 4-step lightMarch per sample at 0.6 scale (~0.75 Mpx) every frame, plus PMREMGenerator.fromScene every 5 s (6 cube faces + prefilter) that produces a periodic hitch.
Post: HalfFloat 4x MSAA scene target (~66 MB colour + depth) resolve, aerial-perspective blit, bright pass, 3 bloom levels x (downsample + 2 blurs), composite = 11 full-screen passes.

Vegetation geometry: canopies are merged icosahedron puffs (detail 1) and 20-segment lofted palm trunks with double-sided alpha-to-coverage fronds; instance counts thin only past 2 km, so trees supply most of the triangle budget.

Draw-call granularity: InstancedMesh per (kind x 1.5 km tile) for 9 building kinds and per (type x variant x 4 km tile) for plants, then multiplied by 3 cascades; WebGL2 per-call CPU cost (~5-15 us) makes 1,300+ calls an 8-20 ms JS/driver load by itself.

Hard horizon seam and hard shore edges (water discard at depth < -0.05, horizonFade cutoff for clouds) in every exterior frame; hard steps in water depth colour from the height texture (island-pass, night)
Static per-pixel cloud dither at 0.6 render scale plus aliasing/shimmer on masts, containers, window lights and sun glitter

Mirrored registration decals and glass/geometry errors on the aircraft (stepped glass outline, black slab intersecting glass, wing-cabin gap, prop-hub light sorting error), and a land-contact model with no forward support that nose-overs on touchdown
summary.flightModelVerdict: The aerodynamic envelope is plausible for a 2.3 t DHC-2-class floatplane (stall 53-57 kt, cruise 109-138 kt, climb ~750 fpm, turn rate within 5% of theory). Control authority is excessive (steady roll rate ~146 deg/s at 60 m/s; 27 deg pitch-up with a +3600 fpm zoom in 4 s from cruise), post-stall behaviour is too benign and under-damped, the ground model has no forward support so any land contact nose-overs, there is no crash/reset state, and the water contact geometry is 7-17 cm below the visual hull while the rendered frames show the hull entirely above the water. The chase camera has a vector-aliasing bug that displaces its look target by 6x the spring acceleration.
summary.performanceVerdict: Current structure is estimated at 25-40 FPS on a GTX 1660 / RX 6600-class GPU at 1080p (CPU draw-call bound with 1,300-1,600 WebGL calls and GPU-bound on water + shadows). After the reductions: ~500-650 calls, 3-4 M triangles, ~10-12 ms GPU, 60 FPS plausible with headroom for spray and wakes. Real-GPU FPS was not measurable on this VM: frames were rendered by SwiftShader (CPU) and 'renderMs' only measures JS submission time; category 27 is scored from draw calls, triangles, memory and pipeline structure.
